findings.title: derive manufactures FormalProof without checking entailment
findings.evidence: Lines 223-240 check modality and premise verification only; lines 248-253 clone any goal and format premise text as a proof term. FormalProof is accepted for reproducibility/confidence at 179-195 without interpreting that term.
findings.trigger: Call derive with a verified epistemic premise A and an unrelated epistemic goal B with Provenance, Reproducibility, Confidence and Completeness obligations.
findings.impact: Returns a FormalProof that verify accepts for B although A does not entail B. This is an unsound proof API, not evidence of a protected runtime effect bypass.

findings.title: Deduplicate statements by modality as well as content
findings.evidence: seen_content stores only js.statement.content although Modality is a semantic field (45-49) and derive requires a Deontic premise (223-230).
findings.trigger: Optimize two individually verified statements sharing content, first Epistemic then Deontic.
findings.impact: Drops the Deontic premise; a subsequent Deontic derivation that previously passed fails HumeViolation, violating stated conservativity at 262/267.

findings.title: Freshness obligation never checks observation age
findings.evidence: has_freshness returns true for every non-Conjecture justification, including Observation timestamp 0. orchestrator.rs:67-88 accepts caller timestamps, calls verify and persists the observation. bindings.rs:179-182 constructs timestamp 0 and invokes verify.
findings.trigger: Verify or inject an arbitrarily old Observation carrying Obligation::Freshness.
findings.impact: The freshness guard passes stale observations and persists them as verified knowledge; no age policy or current-time comparison is performed.

findings.title: Reject expert slices larger than the configured active budget
findings.evidence: Eviction loop runs only while _prefetched_keys is nonempty; lines 177-180 append a slice and increment bytes even if that single byte_length exceeds max_active_ram_bytes.
findings.trigger: Configure a 1 KiB budget and a slice of 2 KiB, then prefetch it into an empty pool.
findings.impact: Internal active_resident_bytes exceeds the configured ceiling immediately. The counter already fails its advertised bound; actual RSS is not measured or certified here.

findings.title: Read path copies complete expert outside active-byte accounting
findings.evidence: read_expert_bytes slices mmap and returns bytes without testing max_active_ram_bytes or changing _active_resident_bytes; accounting is confined to prefetch_layer_experts.
findings.trigger: Call read_expert_bytes for a large slice without prefetching, or retain repeated results.
findings.impact: Allocates expert-sized byte buffers beyond the accounting/budget policy and contradicts zero-copy/strict-RAM claims. No measured hardware ceiling is asserted.

findings.title: Extension audit targets a package path absent from this checkout
findings.evidence: EXT_DIR is REPO_ROOT / babylon60 / extensions; caller_dirs uses the same obsolete root at 58-61. Filesystem metadata inspection found babylon60 and babylon60/extensions absent. Lines 46-48 return without a failure exit.
findings.trigger: Run the audit from this repository layout.
findings.impact: Skips extension reachability entirely and exits successfully, so its output cannot serve as a working pruning/quality gate.

findings.title: Ablation violation metric is hardcoded for the gated condition
findings.evidence: Conditions 0/1 compute synthetic violations (52/78); condition 2 always emits 0. spinal_gate.py:91-97 samples proposed costs and throws when is_viable is false, which is caught at benchmark lines 103-105.
findings.trigger: The gate encounters a nonviable reading and throws SpinalPainException.
findings.impact: Benchmark records zero violations despite observing a nonviable reading, while baselines use different synthetic definitions. Reported between-condition violation comparison is structurally biased; this is an example benchmark, not a validated empirical agent evaluation.

findings.title: Written confirmation is described as a substitute for hardware attestation
findings.evidence: Step 2 permits Touch ID or confirmacion explicita imperativa; canonical .babylon60rules requires hardware attestation tied to the real hash for protected runtime transactions.
findings.trigger: An operator/agent follows this module to release a financial mutation using textual confirmation alone.
findings.impact: Procedure instructs a weaker authorization path than the canonical contract. This is a documentation conflict; no execution consumer or working runtime bypass was established.
